claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my child Alex, who's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on their current situation. Child Benefit usually stops when a child turns 16, but can continue until they're 20 if they remain in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, T-levels, or Scottish Highers) or enrolled in an approved training course?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education - doing A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you. A-levels count as approved education, so that's helpful for Alex's eligibility.

I have a couple more questions to confirm your circumstances:

**Are you responsible for Alex? This means Alex lives with you, or you contribute towards the cost of looking after them (at least the same amount as the current Child Benefit rate).**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you or Alex subject to any immigration controls (for example, do you have a visa that says "no recourse to public funds" or are there any restrictions on your stay in the UK)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, we don't have any immigration restrictions - we're UK residents.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

One final question:

**Does anyone else receive Child Benefit for Alex, or is there any other person who might also be claiming for them?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- ✅ Alex is under 20 years old (18)
- ✅ Alex is in approved education (A-levels)
- ✅ Alex lives with you, so you are responsible for them
- ✅ You are UK residents with no immigration restrictions
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of the assessment:

**Alex (age 18)** ✅ **Eligible**

Although Child Benefit normally stops when a child turns 16, you can continue to receive it for children under 20 who remain in approved education or training. Since Alex is:
- Under 20 years old
- Studying A-levels (which counts as approved education)
- Living with you (meaning you're responsible for them)
- Not being claimed for by anyone else
- And you have no immigration restrictions

...all the eligibility criteria are met.

You can apply for Child Benefit through the official government channels. If you're not already receiving it for Alex, you may want to apply as soon as possible, as claims can usually only be backdated for up to 3 months.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
